name: Data Analysis
tagline: Ask questions of your connected data, then check the query and results.

useCases.title: Ad hoc data pulls
useCases.description: Turn a Slack request into a query against the warehouse, run it, and return the table plus the SQL for review.

useCases.title: Metric investigation
useCases.description: Ask why a KPI moved; the agent slices by dimension, compares periods, and finds the segments behind the change.

useCases.title: Dashboard summaries
useCases.description: Generate a plain-language narrative of what a dashboard shows this week, with the numbers and deltas called out.

useCases.title: Data quality checks
useCases.description: Scan a table for nulls, duplicates, and outliers, and explain which rows look wrong and why before they reach a report.

useCases.title: Recurring reports
useCases.description: Schedule a workflow that runs the same queries each Monday and posts the formatted summary to a channel.

useCases.title: Query explanation
useCases.description: Paste a complex SQL query and get a clear breakdown of joins, filters, and what each CTE computes.

faq.q: Can it connect to my database?
faq.a: Yes. Connect Postgres, your warehouse, or BI tools through MCP or Connections, and the agent queries your live data.

faq.q: Will I see the query it ran?
faq.a: Yes. Review the SQL behind an answer, and the Gateway logs the model calls that produced it, so you can check the logic before trusting a result.

Yes. With a local model, customer data stays on your machine. For cloud models, Gateway rules can block or redact personal data and log each call. Analytics and crash reports are on by default and can be turned off.
